mainTopic: Why a יבמה waits three months before חליצה, and who must support a יבמה while she waits
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the משנה, where רבי יוסי says a widow may not become betrothed during the three months because she is mourning. The גמרא then asks why a יבמה may not do חליצה in the first three months, when only יבום risks the Torah prohibition of אשת אח. It first tries to use this to disprove רבי יוחנן, who holds that חליצה with a pregnant woman counts. It rejects that attempt and offers two reasons for the wait in turn: fear of confusion about her fitness to marry a כהן, and loss of her מזונות. Each reason fails for some type of woman. In the end the גמרא relies on רבי יוסי, who learns from ״ואם לא יחפץ״ that only a woman fit for יבום can do חליצה. רב חיננא challenges this from doubtful cases, such as two sisters, where a woman does חליצה but not יבום. The גמרא answers that the three-month wait is a fixed rule that even applies to a קטנה, so a woman in those months is truly unfit for יבום. The amud then covers who must support a יבמה, including the ruling that a woman waiting for a minor יבם gets nothing. It closes with a ברייתא that a woman who did חליצה within three months must still wait three months.

steps.title: End of the משנה: because of mourning
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the משנה give mourning as the reason for the widow's waiting rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The widow must hold off] because of the mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה, giving mourning (איבול) as the reason for the widow's waiting rule. Next, the גמרא begins discussing the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה is on the previous page. These words finish its last clause, the view of רבי יוסי: all women may become betrothed during the three months except a widow, because she is still mourning her husband. This is a separate reason from the worry about a possible pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning; the period of grief for a deceased husband

phrases.english: because of the mourning.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the משנה that began on the previous page; it is about a widow who must hold off while she mourns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow's waiting rule is based on mourning for her husband.

steps.title: No יבום makes sense, but why no חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts why a possibly pregnant יבמה cannot do יבום, but asks why she cannot do חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense that she should not do יבום. Maybe the baby will turn out to be viable, and then the יבם would have broken the Torah law against his brother's wife. But why should she not do חליצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה forbids יבום during the three months, and then asks why חליצה is forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dead brother left a living child, there is no מצוה of יבום, and the widow stays forbidden to the brother as אשת אח. So doing יבום while she might be pregnant risks a Torah prohibition. חליצה, though, is only a ceremony with no forbidden relations, so the danger is not clear.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (this part is clear, but...)
A brother's wife, forbidden by the Torah unless there is a מצוה of יבום
She does חליצה, the ceremony that releases her from יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two acts. יבום is marriage to the brother, which is a real איסור if a living child exists. חליצה is only a release ceremony, which is why the גמרא is puzzled.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It makes sense that she should not do levirate marriage:
perhaps the baby will be viable,
and he will have run into the prohibition
of a brother's wife, which is from the Torah.
But that she should not do chalitza, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's rule that a יבמה must wait three months
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason for forbidding חליצה during the first three months?

steps.title: Does this disprove רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's rule disproves רבי יוחנן, who holds that חליצה with a pregnant woman counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a disproof of רבי יוחנן, who said: חליצה done with a pregnant woman is a real חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer its question with a reason that would disprove רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the משנה forbids חליצה because חליצה done during pregnancy simply does not work, even if the baby later dies. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who says it does work if the pregnancy ends without a living child. If this reading is right, רבי יוחנן is disproved.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
A disproof that knocks out an opinion
It is called (counts as) a real חליצה

phrases.english: Let us say this is a disproof
of Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
chalitza of a pregnant woman counts as chalitza.
phrases.notes: He means a case where the baby later does not survive; then her חליצה counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to step 2 that would also challenge רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that חליצה of a pregnant woman is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה forbids חליצה during possible pregnancy, it must be because such חליצה does not work, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Wasn't he already disproved? Then this is another disproof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן was already disproved once, and rephrases: this would be one more disproof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't they already disprove רבי יוחנן one time? Then let us say this too is a disproof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to point out that רבי יוחנן was already disproved from a different source. It then restates the suggestion as an additional disproof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It makes no sense to talk as if this were the first attack on an opinion that already fell. So the suggestion is reworded: this משנה would be a second disproof, on top of the first. The challenge itself stays the same; only how it is framed changes.

phrases.english: But didn't they disprove
Rabbi Yochanan one time already?!
phrases.notes: The earlier disproof came from other sources, discussed before this point.

phrases.english: Let us say that from this too there is a disproof!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִי אוֹתְבִינֵּיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects how step 3's challenge is framed without changing its content
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can we call this a disproof if רבי יוחנן was already disproved?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Call it an additional disproof from this משנה as well.

steps.title: A different reason: she would need an announcement for the priesthood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the disproof. The משנה forbids חליצה because if the baby lives, people would wrongly think she is a חלוצה barred from a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Here this is the reason: maybe the baby will be viable, and then you would need a public announcement to show she may marry into כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the disproof of רבי יוחנן by giving another reason for the משנה. This also answers the question from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby lives, her חליצה was meaningless, so she may still marry a כהן. But people saw her do חליצה and would think she is a חלוצה, who may not marry a כהן. To avoid needing a public announcement (כרוז) to clear her, the משנה says not to do חליצה during the three months at all, and that reason says nothing against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And you will turn out to be (causing)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban on חליצה in the first three months is not because such חליצה fails. It is to prevent confusion: if the baby lives, she could marry a כהן, but people would think she is a חלוצה. So רבי יוחנן is not disproved by this משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The worry here is not that the חליצה would be valid. It is the opposite: if the baby lives the חליצה means nothing, yet onlookers would treat her as a חלוצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic rule can be based on how things look to the public, not only on whether the act works legally. That is how the גמרא keeps רבי יוחנן's view safe from this משנה.

phrases.english: No, here this is the reason:
perhaps the baby will be viable,
and you will end up making her need
a public announcement for the priesthood.
phrases.notes: The announcement would tell people her חליצה meant nothing, so she may still marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the disproof in steps 3-4 and answers the question of step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה disproves רבי יוחנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's ban can be explained by fear of confusion about her status for כהונה, not by the חליצה being invalid.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason for the משנה's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה is avoided during the three months to prevent needing a כרוז to clear her for כהונה if the baby lives.

steps.title: Why not just make a public announcement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason from Step 5: let her do חליצה now, and if the baby lives, announce that the חליצה did not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her do חליצה, and if needed, require a public announcement for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the last step. It says a public הכרזה could easily clear up any wrong impression.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said people would wrongly think she is a חלוצה and forbidden to a כהן. The גמרא asks why that is a problem at all. If the baby lives, we could announce that her חליצה meant nothing and she is still allowed to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: let us require for her (an announcement)

phrases.english: But let us require [an announcement] for her!
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the word 'announcement.' It means: if the baby lives, let us announce that her חליצה did not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the concern given in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The concern that people will wrongly treat her as a חלוצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A public announcement could fix the wrong impression, so the concern does not justify forbidding חליצה

steps.title: Not everyone hears the announcement
steps.stepSummary: An announcement does not reach everyone. Some people who saw the חליצה will miss the announcement and still treat her as forbidden to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there will be people who were at the חליצה but not at the announcement, and they will disqualify her from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an announcement is not good enough, because it will not reach everyone who saw the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חליצה and the announcement happen at different times, possibly with different crowds. Anyone who saw only the חליצה will keep thinking she is a חלוצה. So the three-month wait still makes sense, at least for a woman who is currently allowed to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהונה, meaning marrying a כהן

phrases.english: Perhaps there are some who were at the חליצה
but were not at the announcement,
and they will disqualify her from the כהונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אִיכָּא דְּהָוֵאי בַּחֲלִיצָה וְלָא הָוֵי בְּהַכְרָזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical limitation: the fix does not reach everyone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A public announcement would fully undo any wrong impression
steps.terutzMaskana: Some witnesses of the חליצה will miss the announcement, so the problem remains

steps.title: That reason fails for a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The כהונה reason works for an אלמנה, but a גרושה is already forbidden to a כהן, so why must she wait?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for a widow. But for a divorcée, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the כהונה reason and finds a case it does not cover: a woman whose first husband divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה is still allowed to marry a כהן, so a mistaken 'חלוצה' label would really hurt her. A גרושה is already forbidden to a כהן, so the label changes nothing. Yet the משנה makes her wait too, so the כהונה reason cannot be the full explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well (literally, 'it rests well')

steps.confusionAlert: Here גרושה means a woman who was divorced from an earlier husband and then married another man, who died without children. She now needs יבום or חליצה, but because of the earlier divorce she was already forbidden to a כהן.

phrases.english: This works out well for a widow.
For a divorcée, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח אַלְמָנָה. גְּרוּשָׁה — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Steps 5 and 7 from a case it does not cover
steps.kashyaTarget: The כהונה reason for forbidding early חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גרושה is already forbidden to a כהן, so the reason does not apply, yet the משנה still makes her wait

steps.title: She would lose her support payments
steps.stepSummary: A new reason: doing חליצה early would cost her the מזונות she would otherwise receive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it would cause her to lose her support payments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason that covers the גרושה: early חליצה would hurt her financially.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern now is money, not כהונה. Early חליצה would end her right to מזונות. This reason works even for a woman who is already forbidden to a כהן.

phrases.english: Because it causes her to lose her support payments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 with a new reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that covers the uncovered case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason to wait is the כהונה concern
steps.terutzMaskana: There is also a financial reason: early חליצה would cost her the מזונות

steps.title: That reason fails for a betrothed divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The מזונות reason works for a נשואה, but an ארוסה who was divorced has no מזונות and is already forbidden to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for a married woman. But for a betrothed woman who was divorced, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new reason and again finds a case it does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a נשואה gets מזונות, so an ארוסה has nothing to lose financially. If she was divorced, she is also already forbidden to a כהן. Neither reason so far explains why she must wait three months.

keyTerms.meaning: a betrothed woman (after קידושין, before the wedding)

phrases.english: This works out well for a married woman.
For a betrothed woman who was divorced, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח נְשׂוּאָה. אֲרוּסָה גְּרוּשָׁה — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason of Step 9 from a case it does not cover
steps.kashyaTarget: The מזונות reason for forbidding early חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ארוסה has no מזונות, and a divorced one is already forbidden to a כהן, so neither reason applies to her

steps.title: Turning to רבי יוסי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops both earlier reasons and turns to a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי forbids חליצה within three months. The questioner asks what harm it would do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches: A man once came before רבי יוסי and asked, 'May she do חליצה within three months?' He said, 'She may not.' The man asked, 'Let her do חליצה. What is wrong with that?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'rather' and starts over with a new source, a story about רבי יוסי. This step sets up the reason that will fit every woman, which comes when the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier reasons failed for some type of woman, so the גמרא looks for one that covers everyone. The ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי forbade early חליצה, and the questioner presses him to explain why. His answer, which comes next, will be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is wrong with that?

steps.whyThisMatters: After two reasons failed, the גמרא needs one that explains why every woman, of every type, waits three months.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of רבי יוסי,
as it is taught:
There was an incident with a certain man
who came before רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מַהוּ לַחְלוֹץ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the law about doing חליצה within three?
phrases.notes: 'Three' means three months after the husband died.

phrases.english: He said to him: She may not do חליצה.
So let her do חליצה. What is wrong with that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by dropping the earlier reasons and bringing a new source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reasons with one drawn from a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wait is explained by the כהונה concern or by the loss of מזונות
steps.terutzMaskana: The wait is based on רבי יוסי's ruling, whose reasoning is about to be given

steps.title: רבי יוסי's verse: only someone fit for levirate marriage can do the release ceremony
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers the questioner with the פסוק ״ואם לא יחפץ״: חליצה applies only where יבום could have happened. This gives the rule כל העולה ליבום עולה לחליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read this verse to him: "And if the man does not wish." This implies that if he did wish, he could do יבום. So anyone who is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי explains why חליצה may not be done during the first three months. He reads a פסוק to show that חליצה only works where יבום is also possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to do חליצה 'if he does not wish' to do יבום, which assumes he could have chosen יבום. So חליצה is only for a woman who is fit for יבום right now. During the first three months she is not yet fit for יבום, so she cannot do חליצה either.

keyTerms.meaning: He read this verse about him; he answered the questioner with a פסוק
"And if he does not wish"; the פסוק that introduces חליצה
Levirate marriage: the brother marries his late brother's childless widow
The release ceremony that frees the widow from יבום
Anyone fit for יבום is fit for חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's rule: חליצה is tied to יבום. If a woman cannot do יבום right now, she cannot do חליצה right now either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that חליצה depends on fitness for יבום, is the target of רב חיננא's challenge in the next steps.

phrases.english: He read this verse about him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the person in the ברייתא who asked רבי יוסי what harm early חליצה would do.

phrases.english: "And if the man does not wish"
which implies: if he wishes, he may do יבום.
Anyone who is fit for יבום
is fit for חליצה, and so on.
phrases.notes: The "and so on" means the rule continues: anyone not fit for יבום is not fit for חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised to רבי יוסי in step 11: what harm would early חליצה do?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי forbids חליצה within three months.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״ואם לא יחפץ״ shows that חליצה only applies where יבום is possible, and in the first three months יבום is not yet possible.

steps.title: רב חיננא objects: doubtful cases do חליצה but not יבום
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא brings a ברייתא: הספקות חולצות ולא מתיבמות. Here are women who do חליצה even though they cannot do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא objected: The doubtful women do חליצה and do not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא challenges רבי יוסי's rule with a ברייתא. It speaks of women who do חליצה but not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said חליצה goes only with fitness for יבום. This ברייתא seems to describe women who are not fit for יבום but still do חליצה. The גמרא will next figure out exactly which women the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from an older source
The אמורא who raises the objection
The doubtful ones: women whose status is uncertain

phrases.english: Rav Chinena raised an objection:
The doubtful women perform חליצה
and do not enter into יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just derived in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule כל העולה ליבום עולה לחליצה, and anyone not fit for יבום is not fit for חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says some doubtful women do חליצה but not יבום, so חליצה is not always tied to fitness for יבום.

steps.title: Which doubtful case is meant? Not a doubtful betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'doubtful' means. It cannot mean a doubtful קידושין, because then she could simply do יבום with no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the 'doubtful' women? If you say it means a doubtful קידושין, why can't they do יבום? Let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define the ברייתא's case. It tries the first option, a doubtful קידושין, and rejects it. This sets up the real case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is unclear whether the dead brother was ever married to her, יבום is fine either way. If the קידושין was real, she needs יבום. If it was not, she is just an unrelated woman and he may marry her. So the ברייתא's ban on יבום cannot be about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Asks for the meaning of a term or case
If you say; introduces an option that will be rejected
A doubt whether the betrothal was valid
And there is nothing wrong with that

phrases.english: What are the 'doubtful' women?
If you say it means a doubtful betrothal,
why can't they enter into יבום?
Let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case in רב חיננא's ברייתא so the קשיא can be sharpened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the ברייתא means by הספקות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a doubtful קידושין, since there יבום would be allowed. The real case comes in the next step.

steps.title: The case must be two sisters, and she does the release ceremony
steps.stepSummary: The case must be a man who was מקדש one of two sisters and does not know which. There, יבום is forbidden, yet the ברייתא says she does חליצה, against רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a doubt where he betrothed one of two sisters and does not know which of them he betrothed? And the ברייתא teaches: she does חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the real case behind the ברייתא and finishes רב חיננא's challenge. A woman who cannot do יבום still does חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brother was מקדש one of two sisters, the יבם cannot do יבום with either one. She might be the wrong sister, who is forbidden to him as the sister of the woman tied to him. Yet the ברייתא says she does חליצה, so חליצה is possible without fitness for יבום, which contradicts רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not; introduces the only case that remains
And it teaches; points to the wording of the ברייתא as proof

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with יבום here is not the doubt about marriage itself. The problem is that he might marry the wrong sister, who is forbidden to him.
steps.whatToRemember: The two-sisters case seems to show חליצה without יבום, which challenges רבי יוסי's rule that חליצה depends on fitness for יבום.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not a doubt
where he betrothed one of two sisters,
and he does not know which of them he betrothed?
And it teaches: she does חליצה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, סָפֵק שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ אַחַת מִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the doubtful-קידושין reading in step 14, it gives the remaining case and completes רב חיננא's קשיא from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's rule that whoever is not fit for יבום cannot do חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the two-sisters case יבום is forbidden, yet the ברייתא says she does חליצה, so חליצה does not depend on fitness for יבום.

steps.title: The doubtful-sisters case is not like the three-month wait
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב חיננא's challenge. In the sisters case, the woman is really fit for יבום and only our lack of knowledge holds her back. In the three-month case, even a clear statement that she is not pregnant would not allow יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, if אליהו came and said 'he was מקדש this one,' she would be fit for both חליצה and יבום. Here, if אליהו came and said 'this woman is not pregnant,' would we listen to him and let the יבם do יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חיננא's question from Step 15 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the two sisters, the real wife is truly fit for יבום; we just don't know which one she is, so she still counts as עולה ליבום and can do חליצה. During the three months, the bar on יבום is a fixed rule that does not go away even if we know the facts. So that woman is truly not fit for יבום, and by רבי יוסי's rule she cannot do חליצה either.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are not alike)
If אליהו came and told us. A way of asking: what if the hidden fact became known?
We pay attention to, we listen to

steps.confusionAlert: Both women are blocked from יבום, but for different reasons. With the sisters, the only problem is that we don't know which one he was מקדש. With the three months, there is a fixed rule that stays in force no matter what we know. That difference is what decides whether she can do חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sharpens רבי יוסי's rule. 'Fit for יבום' means the woman herself is fit, even if a doubt about the facts stops us from doing יבום in practice.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, if אליהו were to come
phrases.notes: 'There' is the two-sisters case. 'If אליהו came' just means: imagine the hidden fact became known.

phrases.english: and say that he was מקדש this one,
she is fit for חליצה and יבום.
Here, if אליהו were to come
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the woman still inside her first three months.

phrases.english: and say that this one is not pregnant,
would we pay attention to him,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording that some versions add.

phrases.english: and let her go through יבום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge from Step 15 by showing that the ספקות case is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב חיננא's proof from הספקות חולצות ולא מתיבמות against רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sisters case is blocked only by a doubt about the facts, and the woman is really fit for יבום. The three-month case is blocked by a fixed rule, so that woman is really not fit.

steps.title: Proof from a קטנה that the wait does not depend on the facts
steps.stepSummary: A קטנה cannot become pregnant, yet she must still wait three months. This shows the waiting rule applies no matter what, so even אליהו's word would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a קטנה, who cannot become pregnant at all, still has to wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from Step 16 by pointing to the קטנה, a girl too young to become pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the three-month wait were only about checking for pregnancy, a קטנה would not need it. Since she still waits, the rule is fixed and applies even when there is no chance of pregnancy. So we would not listen to אליהו, and the woman truly is not fit for יבום during those months.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl too young to become pregnant

steps.whatToRemember: The three-month wait is a fixed rule even when there is no chance of pregnancy, as the קטנה shows. So a woman in those months is truly not fit for יבום, and רבי יוסי's rule still stands: no חליצה for her.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קְטַנָּה דְּלָאו בַּת אִיעַבּוֹרֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: For a קטנה, who cannot become pregnant,
and even so she needs
to wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קְטַנָּה דְּלָאו בַּת אִיעַבּוֹרֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in Step 16 that we would not listen to אליהו's word.
steps.raayaObject: The three-month wait applies even when we know there is no pregnancy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known rule that a קטנה, who cannot become pregnant, must also wait three months.

steps.title: Who supports a יבמה during and after the first three months
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the dead husband's estate supports the יבמה for the first three months. After that, neither the husband's estate nor the יבם pays for her food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a יבמה gets her food from her husband's estate for the first three months. From then on, she gets food neither from the husband's estate nor from the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who pays for a יבמה's food while she waits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first three months, the dead husband's estate pays for her food. After that, his estate no longer has to, and the יבם does not have to either, since he has not married her. She is left without support from either one.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for יבום or חליצה
The dead husband's brother, who does יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: The רבנן taught: a יבמה,
for the first three months,
receives food from the husband's estate.
phrases.notes: The 'husband' here is the one who died, so the food is paid out of what he left.

phrases.english: From here on, she does not receive food,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל וְלֹא מִשֶּׁל יָבָם.
phrases.english: neither from the husband's estate nor from the יבם.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יְבָמָה, שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים נִזּוֹנֶת מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the food and support of a יבמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the first three months the husband's estate supports her; after that, neither the estate nor the יבם does.

steps.title: A יבם who runs away from בית דין must support her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds one case. If the יבם was brought to בית דין and ran away, he must support the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood in judgment and ran away, she gets her food from the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a case where the יבם does have to pay for her food: he was brought to בית דין and ran away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the יבם owes her nothing before he marries her. But once בית דין tells him to act and he runs away to avoid doing יבום or חליצה, he becomes responsible for her food.

keyTerms.meaning: He stood in judgment, was brought before בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: The food rule has three parts. First three months: the dead husband's estate pays. After that: no one pays. But if the יבם was brought to בית דין and ran away, he pays.

phrases.english: If he stood in judgment and ran away,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the יבם, brought to בית דין and told to do יבום or חליצה.

phrases.english: she receives food from the יבם's estate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to the rule in Step 18, where the יבם does have to support her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבם who runs away after being brought to בית דין must support the יבמה.

steps.title: What if the יבם is a minor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a יבמה whose יבם is a קטן. Clearly he does not feed her, but does the dead husband's estate?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she falls before a יבם who is a minor, what is the law? From the יבם she gets nothing. But from her husband's estate, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about a יבמה whose יבם is still a child. Who, if anyone, has to feed her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן cannot do יבום or חליצה yet, so she is stuck waiting for years through no fault of her own. The יבם is not responsible because he cannot act. The real question is whether the dead husband's estate should feed her, since his death put her in this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother-in-law who is still a minor
She 'fell before', meaning she became bound to him for יבום
She has no right (here, to food support)
From the husband, meaning from the dead husband's estate

phrases.english: If she fell before a yavam who is a minor
(what is the law?)
phrases.notes: Some versions have this word and some leave it out; the question is asked again below anyway.

phrases.english: From the yavam, she has no support.
From the husband's estate, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the support rules of the ברייתא (steps 18-19) to a case where the יבם is a minor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dead husband's estate must feed a יבמה who is stuck waiting for a minor יבם.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue: one says the husband's estate must support her, the other says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One said she does get support, and the other said she does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement between two אמוראים on the question just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says the husband's estate is responsible, since his death left her stuck. The other view says the estate owes her nothing in this situation. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it:
one said: she has support,
and one said: she does not have support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by recording a dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two views: the estate pays, or the estate does not pay.

steps.title: The ruling: she gets no support
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that she gets no support, because her situation is a penalty from Heaven, not the husband's fault.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is that she does not get support. She was penalized from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute: the dead husband's estate does not feed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that her being stuck with a minor יבם is not something the husband did to her. It is her bad luck from Heaven, so his estate does not have to pay for it.
steps.whatToRemember: A יבמה waiting for a minor יבם gets no food support, not from the יבם and not from the husband's estate, because her situation is a penalty from Heaven.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: she does not have support,
they penalized her from Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute of step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The husband's estate does not support a יבמה stuck waiting for a minor יבם, since her situation is a penalty from Heaven.

steps.title: חליצה within three months still needs a wait
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the brothers did חליצה within the first three months, she must still wait three months before remarrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a יבמה who had חליצה from the brothers within three months must still wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about the waiting period. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the חליצה is done early, she is not free to remarry right away. She must still wait three months, so that if she is pregnant it will be clear whose child it is.
steps.confusionAlert: Doing חליצה early does not shorten the wait. The three months still apply before she can marry someone else.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A yevama for whom the brothers performed halitza
within three months,
needs to wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן יְבָמָה שֶׁחָלְצוּ לָהּ אַחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא on the waiting period, moving away from the support discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who received חליצה within three months of her husband's death must still wait three months before remarrying.
